title: Elon Musk Says Micron Has Been ‘Reasonable’ in Future Pricing Memory Where Others Were ‘Extortionate’ — ‘Customers Won’t Forget’
key_facts: Elon Musk, chief executive of Space Exploration Technologies (SpaceX), said in a post on X on Tuesday 13 Oct that Micron Technology 'has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate'.
He added that this is something 'today's customers won't forget' and that Micron's approach is 'the smart move for long-term customer loyalty'.
He was replying to a post by Nicholas Mugalli, chief executive and principal of World Trade Securities, about a new JPMorgan note on memory and storage.
JPMorgan said demand runs well above supply and models shortages of about 20% in 2026, 19% in 2027 and 15% in 2028.
Micron has 26 long-term customer agreements, up from 16, covering more than 35% of revenue through 2030, and over 75% of fiscal 2027 output is committed.
A Futurum Equities strategist said Micron could turn the goodwill into longer contracts and more market share when supply loosens.
quote_evidence: Micron has been reasonable regarding future memory prices, while others have been extortionate, which is something today's customers won't forget.
He was replying to an X post from Nicholas Mugalli, CEO and principal of World Trade Securities, who had highlighted a new JPMorgan bullish note on memory and storage.
JPMorgan said that the setup for memory is 'meaningfully stronger than 90 days ago,' with demand running well above supply.
why_it_matters_hint: A large memory buyer publicly rewards one supplier and criticises unnamed others for pricing during a shortage.
notes: Full text read from fulltext/C05-08.txt. The article is Benzinga's, carried by Yahoo Finance, so Benzinga is the source and the Yahoo link is the page read. Benzinga's text was partly produced with AI tools and reviewed by editors, as it states.
